arxiv-2104-09575.title: Universal algorithms for computing spectra of periodic operators Thanks: JBA acknowledges support from an Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council Fellowship EP/N020154/1. MM acknowledges support from an Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council Grant EP/T000902/1. FR acknowledges
arxiv-2104-09575.creator: Jonathan Ben-Artzi, Marco Marletta, Frank Rösler
arxiv-2104-09575.description: Abstract . Schrödinger operators with periodic (possibly complex-valued) potentials and discrete periodic operators (possibly with complex-valued entries) are considered, and in both cases the computational spectral problem is investigated: namely, under what conditions can a ‘one-size-fits-all’ algorithm for computing their spectra be devised?

arxiv-2212-06165.title: Impedance responses and size-dependent resonances in topolectrical circuits via the method of images
arxiv-2212-06165.creator: Haydar Sahin, Zhuo Bin Siu, S. M. Rafi-Ul-Islam, Jian Feng Kong, Mansoor B.A. Jalil, Ching Hua Lee
arxiv-2212-06165.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Haydar Sahin, Zhuo Bin Siu, S. M. Rafi-Ul-Islam, Jian Feng Kong, Mansoor B.A. Jalil, Ching Hua Lee. Resonances in an electric circuit occur when capacitive and inductive components are present together. Such resonances appear in admittance measurements depending on the circuit’s parameters and the driving AC frequency. In this study, we analyze the impedance characteristics of nontrivial topolectrical circuits such as one- and two-dimensional Su–Schrieffer–Heeger circuits and reveal that size-dependent anomalous impedance resonances inevitably arise in finite L ​ C LC circuits.

arxiv-2303-16642.title: Tracker alignment in CMS : : interplay with pixel local reconstruction
arxiv-2303-16642.creator: for the CMS Collaboration
arxiv-2303-16642.description: Abstract The CMS silicon tracking system measures the trajectories of charged particles with a hit resolution of the order of microns in the pixel detector and tens of microns in the strip detector. One of the most important inputs for track reconstruction is the precision with which the tracker geometry is known.

arxiv-2306-02721.title: Alternating Parity Weak Sequencing
arxiv-2306-02721.creator: Simone Costa, Stefano Della Fiore
arxiv-2306-02721.description: Abstract A subset S S of a group ( G , + ) (G,+) is t t - weakly sequenceable if there is an ordering ( y 1 , … , y k ) (y_{1},\ldots,y_{k}) of its elements such that the partial sums s 0 , s 1 , … , s k s_{0},s_{1},\ldots,s_{k} , given by s 0 =

arxiv-2403-08668.title: BHAC-QGP : three-dimensional MHD simulations of relativistic heavy-ion collisions I. Methods and tests
arxiv-2403-08668.creator: Markus Mayer, Ashutosh Dash, Gabriele Inghirami, Hannah Elfner, Luciano Rezzolla, Dirk H. Rischke
arxiv-2403-08668.description: Abstract We present BHAC-QGP , a new numerical code to simulate the evolution of matter created in heavy-ion collisions in the presence of electromagnetic fields. It is derived from the Black Hole Accretion Code ( BHAC ), which has been designed to model astrophysical processes in a general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamical description.

arxiv-2406-08517.title: DB3V: A Dialect Dominated Dataset of Bird Vocalisation for Cross-corpus Bird Species Recognition
arxiv-2406-08517.creator: Xin Jing, Luyang Zhang, Jiangjian Xie, Alexander Gebhard, Alice Baird, Björn Schuller
arxiv-2406-08517.description: Abstract In ornithology, bird species are known to have variedit’s widely acknowledged that bird species display diverse dialects in their calls across different regions. Consequently, computational methods to identify bird species onsolely through their calls face critsignificalnt challenges. There is growing interest in understanding the impact of species-specific dialects on the effectiveness of bird species recognition methods.

arxiv-2407-10557.title: The bilateral generalized inverse Gaussian process with applications to financial modeling
arxiv-2407-10557.creator: Gaetano Agazzotti, Jean-Philippe Aguilar
arxiv-2407-10557.description: Abstract . We introduce and document a class of probability distributions, called bilateral generalized inverse Gaussian (BGIG) distributions, that are obtained by convolution of two generalized inverse Gaussian distributions supported by the positive and negative semi-axis. We prove several results regarding their analyticity, shapes and asymptotics, and we introduce the associated Lévy processes as well as their main properties.

arxiv-2410-16825.title: Mathematical models and numerical methods for a capital valuation adjustment (KVA) problem
arxiv-2410-16825.creator: D. Trevisani, J. G. López-Salas, C. Vázquez, J. A. García-Rodríguez
arxiv-2410-16825.description: Abstract In this work we rigorously establish mathematical models to obtain the capital valuation adjustment (KVA) as part of the total valuation adjustments (XVAs). For this purpose, we use a semi-replication strategy based on market theory. We formulate single-factor models in terms of expectations and PDEs.

arxiv-2501-16567.title: Adhesion and Reconstruction of Graphene/Hexagonal Boron Nitride Heterostructures: A Quantum Monte Carlo Study
arxiv-2501-16567.creator: Marcin Szyniszewski, Elaheh Mostaani, Angelika Knothe, Vladimir Enaldiev, Andrea C. Ferrari, Vladimir I. Fal’ko, Neil D. Drummond
arxiv-2501-16567.description: Abstract We investigate interlayer adhesion and relaxation at interfaces between graphene and hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) monolayers in van der Waals heterostructures. The adhesion potential between graphene and hBN is calculated as a function of local lattice offset using diffusion quantum Monte Carlo methods, which provide an accurate treatment of van der Waals interactions.

arxiv-2503-01060.title: Convergence rates for an inexact linearized ADMM for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization with nonlinear equality constraints
arxiv-2503-01060.creator: Lahcen El Bourkhissi, Ion Necoara
arxiv-2503-01060.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider nonconvex optimization problems with nonsmooth nonconvex objective function and nonlinear equality constraints. We assume that both the objective function and the functional constraints can be separated into 2 blocks. To solve this problem, we introduce a new inexact linearized alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm.

arxiv-2503-06414.title: Exponential-polynomial divergence based inference for nondestructive one-shot devices under progressive stress model
arxiv-2503-06414.creator: Shanya Baghel, Shuvashree Mondal
arxiv-2503-06414.description: Abstract Nondestructive one-shot device (NOSD) testing plays a crucial role in engineering, particularly in the reliability assessment of high-stakes systems such as aerospace components, medical devices, and semiconductor technologies. Accurate reliability prognosis of NOSD testing data is essential for ensuring product durability, safety, and performance optimization.

arxiv-2508-11840.title: Construction of an isometric immersion of a bounded, planar region from a framed curve
arxiv-2508-11840.creator: Brian Seguin, Eliot Fried, [6pt] Department of Mathematics, Statistics Loyola University Chicago, Chicago, IL 60660-1537, USA, [6pt] Mechanics, Materials Unit Okinawa Institute of Science and TechnologyOnna, Okinawa, Japan 904-0495
arxiv-2508-11840.description: Abstract We develop a framework for characterizing isometric immersions of simply connected, bounded, planar regions with piecewise smooth boundaries into three-dimensional space. Each immersion is associated with a framed curve along the boundary of the image surface, comprised by a parametrized curve and a unit normal vector.

arxiv-2509-16783.title: Spectral Analysis of the Weighted Frobenius Objective
arxiv-2509-16783.creator: Vladislav Trifonov, Ivan Oseledets, Ekaterina Muravleva
arxiv-2509-16783.description: Abstract We analyze a weighted Frobenius loss for approximating symmetric positive definite matrices in the context of preconditioning iterative solvers. Unlike the standard Frobenius norm, the weighted loss penalizes error components associated with small eigenvalues of the system matrix more strongly.

arxiv-2510-06274.title: Bridging Reasoning to Learning: Unmasking Illusions using Complexity Out-of-Distribution Generalization
arxiv-2510-06274.creator: Mahdi Samiei mm.samiei@sharif.edu, Arash Marioriyad arashmarioriyad@gmail.com, Arman Tahmasebi-Zadeh arman.tahmasebi345@sharif.edu, Mohamadreza Fereydooni mrezafereydooni@gmail.com, Mahdi Ghaznavai mahdi.ghaznavi@ce.sharif.edu, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah soleymani@sharif.edu
arxiv-2510-06274.description: Abstract Recent progress has pushed AI frontiers from pattern-recognition tasks toward problems that require step-by-step, System-2-style reasoning, especially with large language models. Yet, unlike learning, where generalization and out - of - distribution (OOD) evaluation concepts are well formalized, there is no clear, consistent definition or metric for “reasoning ability.

arxiv-2512-24221.title: Node-Kayles on Trees
arxiv-2512-24221.creator: Nuttanon Songsuwan
arxiv-2512-24221.description: Abstract Node-Kayles is a well-known impartial combinatorial game played on graphs, where players alternately select a vertex and remove it along with its neighbors. By the Sprague–Grundy theorem, every position of an impartial game corresponds to a non-negative integer called its Grundy value.

pmc-11466352.title: Prognostic value of morning blood pressure surge in chronic kidney disease
pmc-11466352.creator: Zhilan Ma, Yan Wang, Xiaoyan Guo, Lan Ma, Yonghua Liu, Xiaoling Zhou
pmc-11466352.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This was a retrospective study. This study investigated the occurrence of a composite endpoints (cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, end‐stage renal disease, and death) in 153 patients (aged ≥ 18 years) with a diagnosis of in chronic kidney disease (CKD). Based on morning blood pressure surge (MBPS) defined as ≥35 mm Hg, patients were divided into two groups: with MBPS (n = 50) and without MBPS (n = 103). All patients were followed up for at least 1 year.

pmc-11690746.title: NATIVE AMERICAN CAREGIVING PREFERENCES: HEARING THEIR VOICES
pmc-11690746.creator: Pamela Monaghan-Geernaert
pmc-11690746.description: American Indian and Alaska Native elders have the shortest life expectancy of all non-white groups in the USA (CDC, 2022). Despite this disparity, Native elders experience higher rates of morbidity, often necessitating skilled care. Previous research has indicated that enhancing treatment for AI/AN elders must incorporate cultural considerations (Willging et al. 2021).

pmc-12285343.title: Plug-Assisted Retrograde Transvenous Obliteration for the Treatment of Duodenal Variceal Bleeding - A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-12285343.creator: Kyung Kyu Lee, Jae Yong Park, Woo Sun Choi, Young Youn Cho
pmc-12285343.description: Duodenal varices are uncommon complications of portal hypertension. Although duodenal variceal bleeding is infrequent, it is a life-threatening condition with a high mortality rate. Non-surgical methods for duodenal variceal bleeding include endoscopic band ligation, endoscopic sclerotherapy, transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt, and retrograde transvenous obliteration. On the other hand, an optimal treatment strategy for this rare condition has not been established.

pmc-12552122.title: Comparative analysis of dietary fiber impact on bile acid metabolism and gut microbiota composition in mice
pmc-12552122.creator: Andrea Zöchling, Joana Séneca, Petra Pjevac, Arturo Auñon-Lopez, Qendrim Zebeli, Marc Pignitter, Kalina Duszka
pmc-12552122.description: Dietary fiber is essential for health but remains under-consumed in Western diets. Fiber types differ in their physicochemical properties, which influence gastrointestinal function, bile acid (BA) metabolism, and gut microbiota composition. C57Bl/6 mice were fed control or 10% (w/w) fiber diets containing cellulose, chitin, resistant starch, pectin, inulin, β-glucan, psyllium, dextrin, or raffinose.

pmc-12604313.title: The impact of virtual reality (VR) on pain management in the emergency department: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12604313.creator: Hany A. Zaki, Hussam Elmelliti, Benny Ponappan, Mohammed F. Abosamak, Ahmed Shaban, Amira Shaban, Mohamed Elgassim, Eman E. Shaban
pmc-12604313.description: BackgroundAlthough pharmacological and non-pharmacological therapy are available, pain management in the emergency department (ED) may be difficult. In recent years, virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a practical distraction approach for pain relief, especially in children and adolescents. However, little is known about the efficacy of VR in the ED.

pmc-12640304.title: Impact of expanding allogeneic stem cell transplantation on survival in acute myeloid leukemia: a population-based study
pmc-12640304.creator: Brittany Salter, Alejandro Garcia-Horton, Irwin Walker, Brian Leber, Kylie Lepic, Hira Mian, Anastasia Gayowsky, Gregory R Pond, Hsien Seow, Tobias Berg
pmc-12640304.description: ≥65 [1]. For patients with an estimated relapse risk over 35–40%, consolidation with allogeneic stem cell transplant (alloHCT) is standard of care [2]. Although there is no upper limit of age cutoff, historically, older adults have often been excluded from alloHCT due to concerns regarding treatment-related toxicity (TRM) and non-relapse mortality (NRM).

pmc-12884265.title: The Gut Microbiome and Butyrate Differentiate Clostridioides difficile Colonization and Infection in Children
pmc-12884265.creator: Maribeth R Nicholson, Siyuan Ma, Britton A Strickland, Mia Cecala, Lisa Zhang, Seth Reasoner, Emma R Guiberson, Matthew J Munneke, Meghan H Shilts, Eric P Skaar, Suman R Das
pmc-12884265.description: BackgroundSymptomatic Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) can cause significant morbidity and mortality. Conversely, patients can be colonized with toxigenic C. difficile in the absence of symptoms, termed asymptomatic colonization. We previously demonstrated that the presence and function of C. difficile toxins do not differentiate between asymptomatic colonization and CDI in children, suggesting the influence of other factors.

pmc-13120908.title: Integrated clinicopathological, genomic, and immunophenotypic landscape of renal tubulocystic oncocytoma
pmc-13120908.creator: Wenchi Wang, Hengxing Zhu, Chunyu Chen, Man Sun, Honglong Wang, Yu Tai, Sishan Chen, Zhuo Liu, Bo Fan, Yinghua Li
pmc-13120908.description: BackgroundRenal tubulocystic oncocytoma (RTO) is an exceptionally rare variant of renal oncocytoma (RO) with poorly understood genetic underpinnings. This study aimed to characterize the clinicopathological features and genomic landscape of RTO to enhance diagnostic precision and elucidate its molecular profile.MethodsWhole-exome sequencing (WES) was performed on a pathologically confirmed case of RTO to identify somatic mutations.

pmc-13125064.title: Substance use in adolescence is associated with future cardiovascular disease risk: findings from the national longitudinal study of adolescent to adult health
pmc-13125064.creator: Prince Nii Ossah Addo, Monique J. Brown, Rajat Das Gupta, Amos Apreku, Casey D. Xavier Hall, Sylvie Naar
pmc-13125064.description: BackgroundSubstance use is a prevalent public health issue among adolescents in the United States (U.S.). While it’s a known risk factor for adult cardiovascular disease (CVD), the long-term impact of adolescent substance use on future CVD risk is understudied. This study aimed to (1) characterize substance use patterns in adolescents and (2) examine their association with future CVD risk.

pmc-13525077.title: Globalization of Perturbative Chern–Simons Theory on the Moduli Space of Flat Connections in the BV Formalism
pmc-13525077.creator: Pavel Mnev, Konstantin Wernli
pmc-13525077.description: We study the perturbative path integral of Chern–Simons theory (the effective BV action on zero-modes) in Lorenz gauge, expanded around a (possibly non-acyclic) flat connection, as a family over the smooth irreducible stratum M′⊂M of the moduli space of flat connections. We prove that it is horizontal with respect to the Grothendieck connection up to a BV-exact term.

pmc-13584821.title: Conditional generative models enable targeted exploration of MAX phase design space
pmc-13584821.creator: Jamie Swaine, Cyprien Bone, Prakriti Kayastha, Matthew T. Darby, Ewan Galloway, Keith T. Butler

pmc-13651398.title: Application of CT-guided microcoil localization in thoracoscopic resection of small pulmonary nodules
pmc-13651398.creator: Duwang Qiu, Wei Jiang, Defu Chen, Lei Su, Zhenjia Li, Xiaomei Luan, Fei Gao
pmc-13651398.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo evaluate the clinical value of CT-guided microcoil localization for video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) in patients with small pulmonary nodules.MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted in 100 patients with small pulmonary nodules who underwent VATS.
